commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Merge segment reading.

Fixes #1470 by avoiding the second re-scanning.
Odd ciphertext lengths are padded to a word so the eexec decoder
stays aligned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

Per-segment copies keep an even ciphertext length for the decoder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Check the size.

Fixes https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/568035737, also in #1470.
An odd dictionary still counts its alignment byte after the bounds
check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Three commits in T1_Get_Private_Dict each treat an odd-length PFB eexec private dictionary as needing a single alignment byte. f14b47d pads immediately before t1_decrypt: when single_block is already set it only increments private_len, and otherwise it grows the buffer and the length together and sets the flag. 1af9a5f, after the per-segment copy, does that grow-and-count itself and sets single_block so the pad is recorded as already buffered. c2e0add counts the same byte again once the segment bound has been checked, allocating only when single_block is clear. single_block is not set on the PFB path by any one of these commits alone, so each hunk stays consistent: the allocation and private_len move together and t1_decrypt writes inside the buffer. Any two hunks run in the same call. The earlier one reserves the only spare byte and sets the flag; each later one treats the flag as 'pad already buffered' and increments private_len with no matching FT_REALLOC. t1_decrypt then writes past the heap block from PS_Conv_EexecDecode. Removing or correcting any single hunk leaves the other pair in place, so an odd PFB private dictionary still overflows. Even lengths never enter the adjustments, and PFA keeps in_pfb clear, so those paths are unchanged. A fix has to drop the extra increments in at least two of the three sites, or make every increment grow the buffer.
